text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds strongly outperformed their U.S. counterparts but were nonetheless pulled lower in absolute terms on the day by the quarter-point increase in the U.S. Federal Funds rate on Tuesday.
The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.27, down 0.20 from Tuesday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - Gilt futures endured a volatile session, oscillating in a 20-tick range as trade data, a gilt auction and U.S. durable goods orders figures pulled them this way and that.
The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-7/32, down 10/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French 10-year bond futures settled higher after short-covering kicked in at a significant level at 127.64. Traders said the market appeared to be viewing Tuesday's quarter percent Fed funds rate increase as a preventive measure.
The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.22, up 0.12 from Tuesday's settlement price.
ITALY - Italian bonds ended flat while futures, up a fraction on the day, failed to sustain highs as speculation of a larger than expected mini-budget faded.
The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.37, up 0.16 from Tuesday's settlement price.
UNITED STATES - U.S. government securities prices opened slightly higher as the dollar gained against the yen.
The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-12/32, down 11/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.0 percent.
JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond futures were higher due to buying of cash bonds by investors.
In after-hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.94, up 0.69 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - Government bond markets were weaker after the U.S. raised interest rates by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent and as a result mainstream primary market business remained largely absent.
